findings.problem: Every per-IP cap in the hosted-link design uses a client IP that is really a Cloudflare edge address, and the plan never fixes this. The research called it broken before it ships and a pre-existing security defect that belongs in the PR. The plan's IPv6 /64 truncation and HMAC keys are all derived from that wrong IP. In practice, whole regions share one bucket: kids who made no links get the limit message, and attackers slip past. The same defect already weakens the signup, progress and ROM limiters.
findings.evidence: research[4].verify.designSpecProblems[3]: "Per-IP rate limits will not work behind Cloudflare. getClientIP (lib/rate-limit.ts:151-171) keys on x-real-ip ... that IP is a Cloudflare edge address. Nothing in the repo reads CF-Connecting-IP." Confirmed in the repo: apps/web/src/lib/rate-limit.ts getClientIP returns x-real-ip first. `curl -sI https://hankshits.com` returns `server: cloudflare`. grep finds no CF-Connecting-IP in apps/web/src. The plan's 13.2 says "Caps scoped to the offender: per device, account, and IP (IPv6 truncated to /64 ...)", and the 13.1 cost table bounds worst-case egress at "about $5 (per-IP limits)". Neither 13 nor the section 17 defect table says where the IP comes from.
findings.fix: Add to section 17 and to Phase 7 (or earlier, since it is security scope): fix getClientIP so it uses CF-Connecting-IP only when the connecting x-real-ip is inside Cloudflare's published ranges, otherwise x-real-ip. Add a unit test for spoofed and edge-origin headers. Apply the fix to the existing signup, progress and ROM limiters in the same PR. Say explicitly in 13.2 that the /64 truncation and HMAC keys are computed from that validated address.

findings.section: 3 Evidence (AAC priming row) / 6.4 Audio into the encoder
findings.problem: The plan claims priming compensation is proven to 0.02 ms in both ffmpeg and AVFoundation, and 6.4 builds on exactly that: shift the audio timestamps and let mediabunny write an edit list. The research verified the opposite. An edit list alone reads 0 ms in ffmpeg but -44 ms in AVFoundation for native AAC, and -22.6 ms for the WASM path. Only an edit list plus sgpd/sbgp roll groups reads 0 ms in both. mediabunny does not write roll groups, and the plan never mentions them. As written, the pipeline cannot pass its own 5 ms dual-decoder gate (15.2), and iPhone Photos and Messages play the audio early.
findings.evidence: research[1].verify.verdicts[1] (confirmed): "AAC priming breaks A/V sync differently per decoder family; only elst + sgpd/sbgp roll group reads 0 ms in both". research[1].research.findings[8]: "(b) ... shifted by -2112/48000 (mediabunny writes elst media_time=2112, no roll group): ffmpeg 0 to 1.6 ms, AVFoundation -44 ms". research[1].research.openQuestions[8]: "write AAC priming as elst plus sgpd/sbgp roll group ... upstream in mediabunny (#444) or as a post-finalize moov patch". research[0].verify.verdicts[3] rates the 0.02 ms claim only "partly". The plan's section 3 says "After compensation, A/V matched within 0.02 ms in ffmpeg and AVFoundation" (status proven), and 6.4 says "Audio timestamps shift by -P / 48000". grep finds no sgpd, sbgp or roll group anywhere in the plan.
findings.fix: Correct the section 3 row: 0.02 ms was ffmpeg only, and an edit list alone is -44 ms in AVFoundation. In 6.4, add a step to write the edit list plus sgpd/sbgp roll groups, either upstream in mediabunny #444 or as a post-finalize moov patch in io.worker. Apply it to fast-start clips, Record finalize and editor exports. Add a named unit test for the box writer and a Node fixture test that reads 0 ms in both ffprobe and avcheck.swift. Put this in PR 2.1 scope.

findings.problem: The plan says Tier V WebM output supports hosted links, but its own validator and screener accept only MP4 with avc video and aac audio. Tier V devices have no H.264 encoder, so they cannot make a link at all. The plan also says these devices cannot share files, but 32-bit Chrome on Android can. Meanwhile section 12 hard-codes type video/mp4 and a .mp4 name on every share, so a WebM blob would go out mislabeled. The research asked for a separate WebM share path.
findings.evidence: Plan section 5: "Tier V ... VP8 WebM ... Opus ... These devices cannot share files through a share sheet anyway (Firefox Android has no file share) ... so Download and hosted links work." Plan 13.2: "box-walks the MP4 (fast-start layout, one avc video and at most one aac audio track ...)" and the screener uses an "h264/aac decoder allowlist". Plan 12: "new File([...], 'hanks-hits-<game>-<yyyymmdd-hhmm>.mp4', { type: 'video/mp4' }) with that exact type". research[3].verify.designSpecProblems[20]: "give WebM output a separate share path (the 'video/mp4' file-share contract does not apply to it)". research[0].verify.designSpecProblems[17] recommends WebM for Firefox Android through a hosted link.
findings.fix: Choose one approach and write it into sections 5, 12 and 13. Either (a) extend the validator and screener to accept WebM (a VP8/Opus EBML walk, with vp8 and opus added to the decoder allowlist and the unfurl/og:video behavior stated for WebM), or (b) state that Tier V makes no hosted links and remove the claim. In both cases, give Tier V a share path that uses type video/webm and a .webm name wherever canShare accepts it (32-bit Chrome Android). Add a device-matrix row for 32-bit Chrome Android.

findings.problem: On iPhone, long Record videos have no working way out of the app. WebKit's share path reads the whole file into memory twice, so sharing a multi-hundred-MB recording will get the page killed for memory. Section 12 removes Download on iPhone, and hosted links stop at 50 MiB. The big-file handling in 8.3 covers only Chromium's 50 MiB cap. The research said to measure the iOS ceiling and send large files to a download or a link.
findings.evidence: research[0].verify.designSpecProblems[14]: "ShareDataReader.cpp:52-86 loads the whole file with ReadAsArrayBuffer and copies it into a SharedBuffer ... a 20-minute recording needs about 1 GB of WebContent memory. Measure the ceiling on device, and route large files to a download to Files or to the hosted link." research[0].verify.verdicts[15] correction says the same. Plan 8.3: "Share-time handling for big files: Chromium caps file shares at 50 MiB. Over that, the kid picks Trim, a smaller copy ..., Download (no cap), or a hosted link." Plan 12, iPhone row: "No Download button (it lands in Files, which kids cannot find)." Plan 13.1: "Long videos up to 50 MiB get tap-to-play links."
findings.fix: Add an iOS share-size ceiling to the Phase 0 lab (the largest file that shares without jetsam on the oldest supported iPhone). In 8.3, apply a per-platform ceiling, not only the Chromium one. Above the iOS ceiling, offer Trim or split into parts under the ceiling (each shared separately), and bring back a coached 'Save to Files' download for that case only. Add a test for the largest clip a kid can make on iPhone.

findings.problem: Editing a saved clip, and making a link copy of one, both need to decode its AAC audio. The PCM ring covers only the last 62 seconds of the live session. iOS 16.4-18.x (Tier W+, about 1 iPhone in 5) has no AudioDecoder, and the plan names no other decode path. So the Sound tab, speed changes, trims and the 9 MB link re-encode have no audio source for any clip older than the ring on those phones.
findings.evidence: research[0].verify.designSpecProblems[21]: "PcmRing covers only the last ~62 s ... Editing a My Clips item later means decoding its AAC, and iOS 16.4-18.x has no AudioDecoder. Add a WASM AAC decoder (FFmpeg aacdec in the same pinned build), or a main-thread decodeAudioData fallback, or persist lossless PCM alongside each saved clip." research[2].verify.designSpecProblems[11]: link export "means a full decode and re-encode on the phone". Plan 6.5: "PCM ring (Int16, 62 s, 11.5 MB) for the editor". Plan 11.4: "Non-destructive: the source clip plus an edit recipe". grep finds no AudioDecoder, aacdec or decodeAudioData in the plan.
findings.fix: Add an explicit audio decode path to 6.4/6.5 and the Tier W+ row. Use FFmpeg aacdec in the same pinned WASM build, lazy-loaded where AudioDecoder is missing, with decodeAudioData as a secondary fallback. Add an iOS 18 simulator E2E that edits and re-encodes a clip saved in an earlier session. Add a Phase 0 lab check that the decode path runs on iOS 18.

findings.problem: The plan keeps the live encoder open through visible pauses. It also pre-renders editor exports in the background, and it re-encodes link copies with the game paused, which is still a visible pause. Each export needs a hardware decoder and a second hardware encoder while the live ring encoder stays open, so an Android phone needs three MediaCodec sessions at once. The research flagged that some SoCs cannot provide this, and it can trigger Chromium's codec reclamation. The plan does not budget or sequence it.
findings.evidence: research[3].verify.designSpecProblems[15]: "On Android that is three concurrent MediaCodec sessions, which some SoCs cannot provide. Close or pause the live encoder while exporting (or export only outside gameplay) and budget the export memory explicitly." research[3].verify.missedIssues[7]: "Editor exports that need re-encoding compete for hardware codec sessions with the always-on ring encoder ... It is not budgeted anywhere." Plan 7.1: "Visible pauses keep the encoder alive." Plan 11.1: "The editor pre-renders in the background." Plan 13.1: "The client re-encodes to fit with the game paused and a progress bar."
findings.fix: Add an export-session rule to section 7. While an export runs, flush and close the live encoder. The ring stays intact, and a new epoch starts when play resumes. Alternatively, probe for the maximum number of concurrent encoder instances at arm time and serialize exports when it is exceeded. Budget export memory (NV12 decode frames plus a second encoder) per device class. Add an E2E test that runs an editor export during a visible pause on an Android device row.

findings.section: 3 Evidence (compositor row) / 7 Performance governor / 16 Phase 0 PR 0.4
findings.problem: The only compositor path that has been measured costs about 15% of the frame budget, but section 7 promises that capture never costs more than 10%. The plan's own evidence therefore says the governor will step Monster Truck-class games down to a lower capture rate on day one. The research proposed moving scaling and compositing off the main thread: transfer VideoFrame(sourceCanvas), which measured 0.04 ms in Chrome, to the worker and composite there in an OffscreenCanvas. That option is not among the Phase 0 paths A, B and C.
findings.evidence: Plan section 3: "A 960-wide compositor cost about 15%." Plan 7: "The guarantee: capture never costs the game more than 10% of its frame rate." research[0].verify.missedIssues[3]: "Unevaluated alternative compositor: transfer VideoFrame(sourceCanvas) to the worker (cheap in Chrome, 0.04 ms measured) and scale and composite there in an OffscreenCanvas. This moves the ~15% main-thread compositor cost off the game thread ... A/B it on iPhone". research[0].verify.verdicts[7] notes that the transfer cost came from a synthetic canvas, not the real compositor. Plan PR 0.4 measures only "VideoFrame cost for compositor paths A/B/C".
findings.fix: Add a path D to section 3 and to PR 0.4: VideoFrame(gameCanvas) transferred to the encode worker, with scaling, HUD and brand composited in a worker OffscreenCanvas. Measure main-thread cost for A through D on desktop Chrome, Safari and the real iPhone. State that the 10% guarantee is reachable with the chosen path, or name the measured per-engine cadence the governor will settle at.

findings.section: 6.2 Frame pacing and timestamps / 7 Governor ladder
findings.problem: The plan's integer vsync stride produces 25 fps at 50/75 Hz, 28.8 fps at 144 Hz and 27.5 fps at 165 Hz. It then fixes the muxer time scale at 120, which is exact only for 30, 24, 20 and 15 fps. At 25 fps each frame lasts 4.8 ticks, so durations round to an uneven 5-5-5-5-4 pattern. That brings back the container judder the stride was meant to remove, and 144 Hz gaming monitors and 50 Hz displays are common. The governor rung '20 or 24 fps, whichever divides the measured refresh rate' is also undefined at 50, 75 and 144 Hz.
findings.evidence: Plan 6.2: "stride = ceil(Hz / 31), so 30 fps at 60/120 Hz, 25 fps at 50/75 Hz, 28.8 fps at 144 Hz" and "The muxer time scale is 120 (exact for 30/24/20/15 fps)." Plan 7: "a lower integer stride (20 or 24 fps, whichever divides the measured refresh rate)". research[0].verify.designSpecProblems[8] chose timescale 120 for the old 30/24/20/15 ladder. research[3].verify.designSpecProblems[5] replaced it with "fps = Hz/ceil(Hz/31) ... L0 should be 25 fps at 50/75 Hz". The plan merged both without reconciling them.
findings.fix: Derive the time scale from the measured refresh rate (for example timescale = round(Hz) or a multiple of it, so every stride of vsync is an exact tick count), or use a microsecond time scale. Define the governor ladder as fps = Hz / k for successive integers k (k = ceil(Hz/31), +1, +2, ...) with a floor near 15 fps. Add a Node fixture test that the frame durations in the container are uniform at 50, 75, 144 and 165 Hz.

findings.problem: Color handling is missing from the plan. Nobody checks which color metadata (BT.601 or BT.709, limited or full range) each platform encoder writes for RGB canvas input, against how it actually converted the pixels. A mismatch makes clips look washed out or oversaturated in Photos and WhatsApp, and that is a 10/10 quality miss on every clip.
findings.evidence: research[0].verify.missedIssues[0]: "Colorimetry: nobody checked the colr/VUI (BT.601 vs BT.709, limited vs full range) that each platform encoder writes for RGB canvas input ... A mismatch shows up as washed-out or oversaturated clips in Photos or WhatsApp. Add a color-bar fixture to the device matrix and set colorSpace explicitly." grep finds no colorSpace, BT.709, colr or color-bar in the plan.
findings.fix: In 5.1, set VideoEncoder colorSpace explicitly (BT.709, limited range) and write a matching colr box. Add a color-bar lab pattern to PR 0.4 and a Phase 6 device-matrix check. Compare decoded RGB against the source bars in both ffmpeg and AVFoundation, on each encoder family (VideoToolbox, MediaCodec, Media Foundation, OpenH264), within a stated delta-E.

findings.problem: The plan says showing the score only when it equals the player's server-side leaderboard best stops a phone number from appearing as a score. That is false. The leaderboard best is itself taken from client-synced progress, which only caps values at 1 trillion, so any signed-in client can post a highScore of 5551234567 and then have it shown. The research required a per-game plausible maximum in addition to the equality check. The plan dropped that half.
findings.evidence: research[2].verify.designSpecProblems[1]: "Show the score only if it is within a per-game plausible max from the registry AND equals the signed-in player's server-side leaderboard best". Repo: apps/web/src/lib/leaderboard-extractors.ts reads the score from client progress data (e.g. "2048": d.highScore). apps/web/src/lib/progress-schemas.ts:16 has MAX_CURRENCY = 1_000_000_000_000. Plan 13.2: "The score shows only when it equals the player's server-side leaderboard best, so a phone number cannot ride in as a 'score'."
findings.fix: Add a per-game plausibleMax literal to metadata.ts, parsed by generate-game-metadata. Show the score on the hosted page only when it is at or below plausibleMax AND equals the server best. Otherwise leave it out and let the video HUD show it. Add a unit test with a 10-digit phone-number score.

findings.section: Appendix A (flappy-bird, hextris, space-invaders, retro-arcade, DOM render kit) vs 10 Privacy / Appendix B
findings.problem: Several Appendix A specs paint the gamer handle into live capture frames: a title chip plus handle in the top band, retro pillarbox bars with the handle, and a handle chip in the DOM render kit. Section 10 and Appendix B settle the opposite: the handle appears only on the end card, never in live frames. A handle burned into encoded ring frames cannot be removed by the editor's 'gamer tag or no name' choice, or by the new 'Show my gamer name ... on clips' profile toggle, on a packet-copy clip. The research also flagged a persistent handle on hosted clips as an open disclosure question.
findings.evidence: Appendix A, flappy-bird: "Top band: the kit title chip ('🐦 Flappy Bird' plus the leaderboard handle)". Hextris: "Top band: title chip '⬡ Hextris' plus the handle." Space Invaders: "Top band: title chip '👾 Space Invaders' plus the handle." Retro Arcade: "Right: the catalog title (null for uploads) plus the handle." DOM kit: "Render kit: ... handle chip (gaming_profiles.handle only, none for guests)". Plan 10: "The gamer tag appears only on the end card, never in live frames." Appendix B rejects "Name watermark on live frames". The platform risks list (plan-research platform.risks) calls handle attribution a disclosure question.
findings.fix: Remove the handle from every Appendix A band, pillarbox and render-kit spec, leaving the game title chip only. Add a unit test that live-frame and replay-frame painter inputs never include the handle, only end-card inputs do. Regenerate Appendix A from the corrected rule so no builder copies the old specs.

findings.problem: Retro Arcade gets local clips, but its catalog includes RPGs whose name-entry screens are drawn by the ROM onto the emulator canvas (7th Saga, Bahamut Lagoon, Arcana). A kid's typed name, or a full name, lands in the clip. This breaks the settled 'no real names in clips' rule. The section 10 source-scan test (input to fillText or CanvasTexture) cannot see text rendered by a ROM, and the pending #25i allowlist is about gore, not naming screens.
findings.evidence: feasibility-2026-09-27.json research[2] (sharing-and-safety).verify.missedIssues[0]: "retro-arcade serves 151 SNES titles (snes-catalog.ts), including RPGs with name-entry screens drawn on the canvas (7th Saga, Bahamut Lagoon, Arcana) ... Any clip ... can carry a kid-typed full name". The plan's section 10 table lists four-wheeler-3d, Oregon Trail, drawing-app and Wordle only. grep finds no name-entry, 7th Saga or Bahamut in the plan. Plan section 2: "No real names in clips."
findings.fix: Add a Retro Arcade row to the section 10 table. Tag catalog titles that have player-name entry, and for those titles either exclude them from clips or suppress capture (SUSPENDED) while the emulator is on a text-entry screen, using a per-title RAM or screen signature. Put that tagging in the same allowlist work as #25i in PR 3.4, with a test that tagged titles never arm capture on their naming screen.

findings.problem: The editor offers a Tall/Wide shape change, but the ring stores frames already composited at one fixed shape per session. Changing shape therefore means either upscaling a letterboxed region (blurry) or cropping an encoded frame, and both are re-encodes. The research asked the plan to pick a design (store un-composited frames plus a HUD timeline, or accept crop/letterbox) and to state the trade-off honestly. The plan does neither. Path B (direct WebGL frames with the HUD kept out of the frame) changes the answer again, and on top of that, path B's 'live overlay strip encoded as a second small region' would not display in Photos or iMessage as a composite.
findings.evidence: research[4].verify.designSpecProblems[8]: "If the ring stores COMPOSITED Tall/Wide frames, 'shape change' can only upscale a letterboxed game region, which looks blurry ... The spec must pick one design and state the tradeoff honestly." research[3].verify.designSpecProblems[0]: "WebKit has no zero-readback way to overlay a HUD" (HUD moves to the end card). Plan 5.1: "Output dimensions are fixed per session". Plan 11.4: "Style (shape Tall/Wide, ...)". Plan section 3, path B: "the HUD moves to a live overlay strip encoded as a second small region, or to the end card."
findings.fix: State in 6.1/11.4 which design is used for each compositor path. For example: the ring stores the game region at the source aspect plus a HUD value timeline, and shape and HUD are composited at export (a re-encode on the export session from finding 6). Or: the shape is chosen before capture, and editor shape changes crop or letterbox with a visible quality note. Drop the 'second small region' option from path B and keep 'HUD to end card' only.

findings.section: 13 Hosted clip links (recipient page, Make a link UX)
findings.problem: Two parts of the link flow have no written design. First, the recipient page: it needs a muted autoplay loop with tap-to-unmute, a read-aloud button (a project rule for young readers, and a hand-built Route Handler page does not inherit the React ReadAloudButton), kid-friendly relative expiry ('gone in 30 days'), and an 'Open in Chrome' handoff for Android in-app browsers, where recipients usually land. Second, the sender side: navigator.share needs a fresh tap, but a link goes live only after upload and screening, so the second tap and the waiting state are unspecified. PR 7.3 lists only 'Make a link UX'.
findings.evidence: research[2].verify.designSpecProblems[23]: "no muted autoplay loop with tap-to-unmute; no read-aloud button ...; no kid-friendly relative expiry ('gone in 30 days'); and no second-tap share step after the async 'live' status (navigator.share needs transient activation)." research[4].verify.missedIssues[4]: "The /c/<slug> recipient page is usually opened inside exactly those browsers, so it needs an 'Open in Chrome' handoff." Plan 12: "Share calls navigator.share ... synchronously in the tap, and never after an await." Plan 13.1 describes the page only in terms of headers and CSP. Plan PR 7.3: "Make a link UX".
findings.fix: Add a 13.4 'Link experience' subsection. Sender: 'Making your link...' progress with kid-word states for uploading, checking, ready and held. When the link is ready, show a Share button that the kid taps again, and write the ready link to My Clips > Links. Recipient: muted inline autoplay loop with a large tap-to-unmute control, a read-aloud button built into the hand-built HTML (speechSynthesis), 'This video goes away in N days', a 'Play this game' CTA, an in-app-browser handoff, and a report link. Add all of these to the /ux and /qa gates for PR 7.3.

findings.problem: The device rows use Jack's adult iPhone, a generic Android phone and a school Chromebook. The configurations kids actually use are missing: a Child Apple Account with Screen Time content restrictions, and a Family Link supervised Android. These can change share-sheet targets, Save to Photos, downloads and site access. The research named them as missing surfaces for this exact feature.
findings.evidence: research[1].verify.designSpecProblems[19]: "The device rows use Jack's adult iPhone. They miss the actual users' configurations: a Child Apple Account with Screen Time content restrictions, a Family Link supervised Android, and a managed school Chromebook (download restrictions, filtered networks)." Plan 15.1, Real devices: "Jack's iPhone (Safari tab, Home Screen app, private tab, Chrome for iOS), an Android phone, a school Chromebook ...". grep finds no Screen Time, Family Link or 'supervised' in the plan.
findings.fix: Add required Phase 6 rows for (a) an iPhone signed in to a Child Apple Account in Family Sharing with typical Screen Time restrictions, and (b) an Android device under a Family Link supervised profile. Run Clip it, Save to Photos or gallery, Share and Download on each, and record evidence. Where a restriction blocks an action, the UI must show a kid-word reason, never fail silently.

findings.problem: The global next.config '/:path*' header rule also matches /c/<slug> and /c/<slug>/embed. That rule sends X-Frame-Options DENY, frame-ancestors 'none' and media-src 'self' blob:. The plan says only that the page 'has its own CSP' and that PR 7.3 ships an embed. It never removes /c/* from the global rule. Next's headers() cannot unset a header that the global rule sets, so the embed is blocked by DENY / frame-ancestors 'none'. If the route's CSP is sent alongside the global one, browsers enforce both, and bucket playback stays blocked by media-src.
findings.evidence: research[2].verify.designSpecProblems[20]: "headers() cannot UNSET X-Frame-Options for /c/:slug/embed, because the global '/:path*' rule also matches ... Either exclude the path with a negative-lookahead source, or rely on CSP3 frame-ancestors overriding XFO". Repo apps/web/next.config.ts:18-35: source "/:path*" sets X-Frame-Options DENY and a CSP with "media-src 'self' blob:; ... frame-ancestors 'none'". Plan 13.1: "has its own CSP with the bucket host in media-src". Plan PR 7.3: "embed".
findings.fix: In PR 7.3, change the global source to a negative lookahead that excludes /c/. Give /c/:slug and /c/:slug/embed their own header rules: the embed gets no XFO and a frame-ancestors list naming the unfurl hosts, and both get media-src with the bucket host. Add header tests that assert exactly one CSP header, the expected frame-ancestors and media-src values, and the absence of XFO on the embed.

findings.section: 1 Summary vs 13.1 cost table / 19 Open questions
findings.problem: The cost numbers disagree with each other. The summary says about $6, $11 and $30 a month at 1k, 10k and 100k links, and a worst-case abuse bill under about $25. The 13.1 table (whose rows sum correctly) says about $5, $7 and $15-25, and a worst case of about $18. Jack decides the hosted-links open question on these figures.
findings.evidence: Plan section 1: "about $6/month at 1,000 links a month, about $11/month at 10,000, and about $30/month at 100,000 ... under about $25/month". Plan 13.1 Total row: "about $5 | about $7 | about $15-25 | about $18, then auto-pause" (e.g. 10k: $1.62 + $0.21 + $5 = $6.83). Plan 19: "They cost about $5-25/month".
findings.fix: Regenerate the summary and section 19 figures from the 13.1 table, or correct the table if the summary uses different assumptions, and state those assumptions (average link size, mix of 30-day and 14-day lifetimes).

findings.problem: Safari's AudioEncoder drops the first 1024 real samples at every encoder start. Offset-only checks miss this, and the plan adds no pre-pad or check. The result is a 21 ms hole or shift at every session start and after every encoder re-creation (a new epoch on iOS resume or on RECOVERING).
findings.evidence: research[1].verify.designSpecProblems[11]: "The Safari AudioEncoder eats the first 1024 real samples (mediabunny #444). Offset-only checks miss this. Add a 't=0 beep present at full 60 ms' lock and a pre-pad-1024 requirement for every encoder start, including restarts after reclamation." grep finds no pre-pad in the plan.
findings.fix: In 6.4, pre-pad 1024 samples of silence (not counted in the timeline) on every AudioEncoder configure. Add the 't=0 beep present at full length' named test to the E2E lab pattern for the WebKit rows.

findings.problem: iOS 16.4-16.x is in Tier W+, but Safari has had StorageManager.estimate() and the 60% quota only since version 17. On those phones, the library cap's '1 GiB if unknown' default can exceed the real origin quota, the Record check 'every 10 s' has no input, and the plan says nothing about handling QuotaExceededError mid-write.
findings.evidence: research[0].verify.designSpecProblems[13]: "Record-mode storage guard depends on estimate(), which Safari only has from 17 ... Provide a quota-probe fallback: write-ahead preallocation or truncate test, plus QuotaExceededError handling alone." research[0].verify.verdicts[19] correction says the same. Plan 8.1: "at most 25% of the quota estimate (1 GiB if unknown)". Plan 8.3: "checked before start and every 10 s".
findings.fix: Where estimate() is missing, run a preallocation probe (write, then truncate) to learn the available space. Treat QuotaExceededError in the IO worker as a normal stop: finalize to the last durable fragment and show kid-word copy. Add an iOS 16.4 simulator test.

findings.problem: 'Memory budget by device class' is never defined for iOS, where navigator.deviceMemory does not exist. The 2 GB iPhones most at risk of a memory kill get the same 60 s ring (about 22 MB of video plus 11.5 MB of PCM plus AAC) as a desktop until the crash breaker has fired at least once.
findings.evidence: research[0].verify.designSpecProblems[12]: "Low-memory policy keys on navigator.deviceMemory, which is Chromium-only (BCD) ... iOS needs its own conservative default, for example keyed on iOS major version or screen class". Plan 6.5: "Memory budget by device class (about 22 MB at 3 Mbps)." grep finds no deviceMemory in the plan.
findings.fix: Define the device-class function in 6.5. On Chromium use deviceMemory; on WebKit use a conservative default keyed on screen class and the AudioEncoder-presence proxy (iOS 26+ means A13+), with a smaller ring on the lowest class. Size it from the Phase 0 jetsam soak.

findings.problem: When the software bridge hands over to hardware, and when an editor smart-cut splices a re-encoded GOP, two encoder instances can emit back-to-back IDR frames with the same idr_pic_id. That violates H.264 7.4.3, and a single-frame GOP makes it more likely. The plan has no rule against it.
findings.evidence: research[0].verify.missedIssues[6]: "consecutive IDRs from two encoder instances need distinct idr_pic_id (H.264 7.4.3). Enforce GOPs of 2 frames or more in card and smart-cut sessions." research[0].verify.verdicts[6] correction says the same. grep finds no idr_pic_id in the plan.

findings.evidence: research[2].verify.designSpecProblems[11]: "It also needs an overshoot retry loop, because hardware VBR encoders routinely beat a 3% margin". research[2].verify.designSpecProblems[12]: "The client should persist the job in IndexedDB and resume it on return." summary:
I checked every verify.designSpecProblems item (119) and every verify.missedIssues item (60) across the 5 tracks in plan-research-2026-09-27.json, plus all 28 platform.risks entries, against sections 1-19 and the Appendices. About 80% are properly addressed. Examples: Quality({bitrate}), the NullTarget harness removal, the PLL resampler, synthesized silence, keyframe-start clips, the split into encode and IO workers, Web Locks, the owner-purge rules, removing the Record cap, the private-window fallback, full-frame screening, presigned PUT with a signed checksum, the single-region bucket, the Route Handler clip page, no-store 302s, the separate legal-hold bucket, TOTP, the Retro Arcade hosting 'off' policy, the Phase 0 privacy notice, the 320 px header fix, the runtime lab flag, the non-Mac pre-push skip, and the dual-decoder 5 ms / ITU thresholds.

**The most serious gap is critical.** The plan's per-IP abuse caps run on getClientIP, which returns the Cloudflare edge IP (apps/web/src/lib/rate-limit.ts). The plan never fixes this, and section 17 does not list it as a pre-existing defect.

**Major contradictions and omissions:**
- **AAC priming:** the plan claims 0.02 ms in both ffmpeg and AVFoundation, but the research confirmed that an edit list alone reads -44 ms in AVFoundation. Roll groups (sgpd/sbgp) are required and missing.
- **Tier V WebM:** the plan says hosted links work there, but the validator is MP4/avc/aac-only and every share hard-codes video/mp4.
- **iPhone long recordings:** share loads the file into memory twice, Download is removed, and links stop at 50 MiB, so long videos have no way out.
- **No AAC decode on iOS 16.4-18:** saved clips cannot be edited and link copies cannot be re-encoded on those phones.
- **Three concurrent codec sessions** during exports, because the live encoder stays alive through visible pauses.
- **Compositor cost:** 15% measured against a 10% guarantee, and the research-proposed worker-side compositing is not among the Phase 0 paths.
- **Timescale 120** does not fit the 25/28.8 fps strides, which brings back judder.
- **Color handling** (colorSpace/colr) is missing entirely.
- **Score channel:** the 'equals leaderboard best' guard still lets a phone number through, because leaderboard bests are client-declared up to 1e12.
- **Handle in live frames:** Appendix A paints the gamer handle into live frames, against section 10 and Appendix B.
- **Retro Arcade RPG name-entry screens** can carry kid-typed names (from the feasibility research).
- **Editor Tall/Wide** versus a fixed-shape composited ring is undecided.
- **Link flow UX:** the recipient page and the Make a link flow have no design.
- **Child accounts:** no Child Apple Account or Family Link device rows.
- **Global headers:** the '/:path*' XFO DENY and CSP rule is never excluded from /c/*.

The remaining gaps are minor: the cost-figure mismatch between the summary and 13.1, the Safari 1024-sample drop, quota handling before Safari 17, the undefined iOS memory class, IDR splicing, stale browser versions, setInterval auto-discovery, harness and edge-test gaps, the link re-encode retry and upload resume, kid-built screening calibration, silent app opt-outs, the persist() policy, and the dependency of 'Send to a phone' on Phase 7.

One disputed research item is not a plan defect. A verifier said Chrome desktop share is Windows/ChromeOS-only, but current MDN BCD lists Chrome 128+ with full support, so the plan's 'macOS 128+' is correct.

I found 16 problems in sections 4-9 (1 critical, 10 major, 5 minor), checked against the repo, mediabunny 1.60.0 source (/private/tmp/hh-clips/node_modules/mediabunny), Chromium and Firefox source, BCD 8.1.3 and the research JSON.

The critical one is encoder "epochs". The plan says the clip assembler supports splicing across encoder changes (software bridge to hardware, a resolution step down, recovery). But mediabunny writes only the first packet's encoder config into the MP4, so a clip that spans two epochs is either corrupt or silently shorter. The plan also contradicts itself here: 5.1 says output size is fixed per session, while the section 7 ladder changes resolution.

The major problems:
- Timing math is inconsistent: timescale 120 cannot represent the 25 and 28.8 fps rates the stride formula produces.
- Appendix A asks for 60 fps capture, which the 30 fps engine and the level-3.1 codec strings do not allow.
- Frame-counter timestamps drift against audio when a game misses vsyncs.
- The keyframe-starvation fallback does nothing on Chromium (Chromium treats an identical configure() as a lightweight options change, so no keyframe comes out).
- Tier V's 1 s fragment ring cannot work on Firefox, which hard-codes a 10 s VP8 keyframe interval.
- Mixing audio from iframe AudioContexts is not specified, and the plan uses two different clock-anchor methods.
- Path B's "second small region" HUD has no possible mechanism.
- The only measured 3D compositor cost (17-19% on an M5) already breaks the 10% budget, but section 3 labels it "proven".
- The editor's decode, codec-session and worker needs for saved clips are missing.
- iOS big-file sharing runs out of memory.

The minor ones: Safari private windows also reject IndexedDB Blobs; the tier table misses some browsers inside the floor; the "no edit list" claim is wrong for audio; the pause-cut domain is ambiguous; the DOM-replay AAC path skips the plan's own ASC and WASM rules.

findings.section: 5.1 Encoder configuration / 6.5 Rings and clip assembly / 7 Ladder / 7.1 / 8.3 Record mode
findings.problem: The plan relies on clips crossing encoder epochs, but nothing can mux that. 5.1 says the bridge-to-hardware hand-over 'creates a new "epoch", which the clip assembler supports', and 15.1 lists an 'epoch splice' fixture. But mediabunny writes only the first packet's decoderConfig (avcC and coded size) into the track. When a clip crosses into a different config, the packets after the splice are decoded against the wrong SPS/PPS or the wrong dimensions. 7.1 accepts the other outcome ('closing it risks a new avcC that shortens the next clip'), so the plan contradicts itself: either clips are corrupt or they are silently shorter, which breaks the 'never silent' rule in 6.5. The epoch sources are exactly the ones that change the avcC: a different (software) encoder for the cold-start bridge, the governor's 'one resolution step down (new epoch)' and '480p' low-power rung, and the RECOVERING recreate. The ladder also contradicts 5.1 'Output dimensions are fixed per session'. Record mode 'tees the same encoded packets into a fragmented MP4' across these same epochs, with no rule for how the parts join. The bridge is also internally inconsistent. It is 'a software bridge encoder at the same size', while the same section says 'if only software passes, drop one preset step and cap at 20 fps'. On WebKit and on 32-bit ARM Chrome there is no software rung at all (research storage-perf-lifecycle DSP 2).
findings.evidence: /private/tmp/hh-clips/node_modules/mediabunny/dist/modules/src/isobmff/isobmff-muxer.js:207-211: getVideoTrackData returns the existing trackData, and later meta.decoderConfig values are ignored. plan-research encoding-pipeline verify.verdicts[6]: byte-identical avcC is proven only for two instances with the identical config, and isobmff-muxer.ts:401-420 uses the first decoderConfig only. storage-perf-lifecycle DSP 3: 'mediabunny freezes the track config at the first packet. The latest-segment rule then silently shortens Clip it!'. GAMEPLAY_CLIPS.html:274-275 and 337.
findings.fix: Add an explicit epoch policy to 6.5. (1) Keep the coded size constant for the whole session. Do governor resolution steps by scaling the content inside the fixed coded frame, so the SPS never changes size. (2) Classify every epoch boundary as either 'identical avcC' (splice allowed, verified by a byte compare at run time) or 'different avcC'. For a different avcC, either re-encode the older part through the current encoder at clip time, or cut the clip to the newest epoch and show the real seconds on the button and in the toast. (3) Record mode: roll to a new part at every avcC change, and re-encode the smaller part at finalize. (4) Remove 'the clip assembler supports' until (2) exists. Make the Node 'epoch splice' fixture use two different avcCs and assert that the output decodes in ffmpeg and AVFoundation. (5) Make the bridge rule match 5.1: the bridge runs at the software preset (one step down, 20 fps) and therefore always takes the re-encode or cut path. On WebKit and 32-bit ARM Chrome, there is no bridge. State what happens there.

findings.problem: 'The muxer time scale is 120 (exact for 30/24/20/15 fps)' contradicts the stride rule in the bullet just above it, which produces 25 fps (50/75/100 Hz), 28.8 fps (144 Hz), 27.5 fps (165 Hz) and 22.5 fps (90 Hz, stride 4). In mediabunny, setting frameRate snaps every timestamp to 1/frameRate. With 120, 25 fps frames land on alternating 5/5/5/5/4-tick durations (41.7/33.3 ms), and 28.8 fps on 4/4/4/4/5. That writes into the file the same judder the stride design was meant to remove. The ladder 'then a lower integer stride (20 or 24 fps, whichever divides the measured refresh rate), then 15 fps' has no valid rung at 50, 75, 90, 144 or 165 Hz: neither 20 nor 24 divides those rates, and 15 does not divide 50 or 144. The 3D group note (Appendix A, line 2400) still says 'Adapt fps down (30 to 24)', which judders at 60 Hz.
findings.evidence: mediabunny output.d.ts:177-182: 'If set, all timestamps and durations of this track will be snapped to this frame rate'. isobmff-muxer.js:254: timescale = den of 1/frameRate. With frameRate unset, GLOBAL_TIMESCALE = 57600 (isobmff-muxer.js:22), which is exact for 24/25/30/60/28.8/22.5/14.4. The two research tracks disagree: encoding-pipeline DSP 8 ('Use frameRate 120 ... or omit it') and storage-perf-lifecycle DSP 5 ('integer vsync stride ... 25 fps at 50/75 Hz, 28.8 at 144 Hz'). The plan kept both without reconciling them. GAMEPLAY_CLIPS.html:295, 297, 337.
findings.fix: Do not pass frameRate to addVideoTrack. That uses the 57600 timescale, and its worst-case rounding at 27.5 fps is under 9 µs. Or compute a per-session timescale that is exact for every rung reachable at the measured Hz. Define the ladder as successive integer strides of the measured refresh (fps = Hz/k for k = base stride, base+1, ...), and show the rungs per refresh rate in a table (60: 30/20/15; 120: 30/24/20/15; 144: 28.8/24/20.6/18; 50: 25/16.7/12.5). Replace 'then 15 fps' and the '30 to 24' group note with that table.

findings.problem: The per-game specs require 60 fps capture that the engine sections cannot produce. Appendix A sets fps: 60 in useClipSource for arkanoid, asteroids, blitz-bomber, breakout, dino-runner and endless-runner. It gates arkanoid on 'recording at 60 fps must hold p95 frame time under 16.7 ms', and asteroids' smoke test asserts 'a 960x960 MP4, 60 fps'. Snake's offline render is '60 fps (not 30)'. Section 6.2 caps capture at stride = ceil(Hz/31), about 30 fps. 5.1 budgets bitrate 'at 30 fps', and the 6.5 ring budget (22 MB/60 s) assumes that rate. 5.1's codec strings are all level 3.1 (avc1.64001f/4d001f/42001f), whose MaxMBPS of 108,000 allows 720p or 960x960 only up to 30 fps. 720x1280@60 or 960x960@60 is 216,000 MB/s, which needs level 3.2 (0x20).
findings.evidence: GAMEPLAY_CLIPS.html:775, 875, 948, 1103, 1174, 1241 (fps: 60); :943 ('a 960x960 MP4, 60 fps'); :770 (arkanoid 60 fps gate); /tmp/gc_plan.txt:2124, 2430 (snake 60 fps). Plan :271 (codec order) and :295 (stride). ITU-T H.264 Table A-1: level 3.1 MaxMBPS 108000, level 3.2 216000.
findings.fix: Pick one model and write it into 6.2. If 60 fps capture is wanted for fast 2D games, add a 60 fps preset with level 3.2 codec strings (avc1.640020/4d0020/420020), doubled bitrate and ring budgets, a governor ladder that starts at 60, and a Phase 0 measurement of 60 fps readback on iPhone. If it is not wanted, rename the useClipSource field (for example simHz) so it is clearly the game's simulation rate, and change the asteroids/arkanoid/snake tests to assert 30 fps. Either way, choose the codec level from (width, height, fps), not from a fixed list.

findings.problem: The fallback 'If a device ignores keyframe requests ... the engine re-configures with the identical config every 1 s, which keeps the avcC byte-identical and seamless' does nothing on Chromium. Blink routes an identical-config configure() through CanReconfigure, then ProcessReconfigure, which calls Flush() and ChangeOptions() on the same media encoder. The VEA adapter only calls RequestEncodingParametersChange(bitrate, framerate). No new MediaCodec is created and no IDR is forced. So on the exact devices this targets, the video ring still cannot evict its single growing GOP (research DSP 6: 'memory grows without limit', up to 100 s of pre-roll). The fallback also adds a full encoder flush every second, which stalls the pipeline and drops frames.
findings.evidence: chromium third_party/blink/renderer/modules/webcodecs/video_encoder.cc:992-1007 (CanReconfigure: same codec, profile, level and hw_pref → reconfigure) and :1492-1575 (ProcessReconfigure → media_encoder_->Flush → ChangeOptions). media/video/video_encode_accelerator_adapter.cc ChangeOptionsOnAcceleratorThread → accelerator_->RequestEncodingParametersChange only. encoding-pipeline verify.designSpecProblems[6]. GAMEPLAY_CLIPS.html:273.
findings.fix: Replace the fallback with one that forces a new session: reset() plus configure(), or close the old VideoEncoder and create a new one with a short overlap. Measure its cold-start cost and avcC identity on the Android device in Phase 0 (add 'keyframe-starved recovery' to the PR 0.4 lab list). Separately, cap the ring by bytes even inside a GOP. When the cap would cut the only GOP, fall back to 'clip starts with a re-encoded leading partial GOP' (the editor's smart-cut), and never let the GOP grow without a bound.

findings.problem: Tier V promises 'Instant replay: Yes (fragment ring)', and tier M relies on '1 s keyframe-led fragments'. Firefox's MediaRecorder VP8 encoder hard-codes a 10 s keyframe interval, and no web API changes it. A Firefox Android fragment ring therefore has 10 s granularity, so 'Clip it!' starts up to 10 s early (or cuts a GOP), not 'at most 1 s longer'. The 'two staggered recorders' patch only halves that. It doubles software VP8 encoding next to the game on low-end phones, and it contradicts 7.1's 'never a second hardware encoder'. Keyframe-led 1 s fragments were proven only on Safari 26.5 (verify [14]). Chromium's MediaRecorder keyframe cadence is also left unspecified.
findings.evidence: mozilla firefox dom/media/encoder/VP8TrackEncoder.cpp:29 'constexpr int DEFAULT_KEYFRAME_INTERVAL_MS = 10000'. mKeyFrameInterval is set only in the constructor (:151) and forced at :530-538. encoding-pipeline verify.verdicts[14] ('proven only on Safari 26.5'). GAMEPLAY_CLIPS.html:263-266.
findings.fix: For tier V, design the ring as rotating recorders. Stop and start a MediaRecorder every N seconds (each start begins with a keyframe and its own WebM header), overlap two recorders only across the hand-off, and let mediabunny concatenate the segments (VP8 has no out-of-band config, so there is no avcC issue). Measure N and the CPU cost on a real Firefox Android phone in Phase 0. Or state honestly that Firefox Android clips start at the last keyframe, up to 10 s earlier. For tier M on Chromium, set videoKeyFrameIntervalDuration where the browser supports it, and probe the observed keyframe spacing at arm.

findings.problem: 6.4 describes one PCM stream: one tap, one (performance.now, ctx.currentTime) anchor stream, one PLL and resampler, and 'contiguous, sample-counted timestamps'. But 6.3 keeps a separate AudioContext in each iframe realm ('redirects destination to a tapped bus in that realm'). Four-Wheeler Adventure and Retro Arcade then need a second tap with its own clock, time origin and possibly its own sample rate, mixed into one AAC stream. The per-stream PLL, the mixer, and the watermark rule for a suspended or dead stream (research DSP 26: 'or the whole AAC ring stalls waiting for a dead stream') are not specified. Appendix A also maps the foreign taps with ctx.getOutputTimestamp(), while 6.4 anchors on currentTime. getOutputTimestamp().contextTime is the sample now at the output device, so it lags currentTime by the output latency (100-250 ms on Bluetooth/AirPods). Mixing streams anchored the two ways shifts them apart by that much, well past the -125 ms bound in 15.2. Appendix A's 'bus.connect(tapNode), with no output to destination' also contradicts 6.3's 'zero-gain sink so the tap is always pulled'. Retro Arcade is specified two different ways: a constructor shim (6.3) versus kit.attachForeignTap(AL.currentCtx.gain, win) on EmulatorJS internals (Appendix A :2028).
findings.evidence: GAMEPLAY_CLIPS.html:307 (constructor shim), :315 (currentTime anchors), :1901-1906 (4WA foreign tap: 'no output to destination', 'clock mapping via ctx.getOutputTimestamp()'), :2028 (retro attachForeignTap + getOutputTimestamp), :2386. storage-perf-lifecycle DSP 18 ('the worker has to mix streams whose clocks are mapped separately'). encoding-pipeline DSP 26. Web Audio spec AudioTimestamp: contextTime is 'the sample frame currently being rendered by the audio output device'.
findings.fix: Add a 6.4.1 'Mixer' subsection. Each tap stream gets its own anchor, PLL, resampler to 48 kHz and ring. Mix in the worker with a per-stream watermark that drops a stream once it is suspended, closed or its realm is unloaded (zero-fill it instead). Use one anchor method for every stream: the tap's own currentFrame or currentTime (production time), converted through performance.timeOrigin for iframe realms. Never use getOutputTimestamp, or subtract baseLatency+outputLatency if you do. Every tap node connects through a zero-gain sink to its realm's destination. Pick one Retro Arcade mechanism and delete the other. Add a Bluetooth-route A/V check to the 15.2 thresholds.

findings.section: 3 / Path B (Direct WebGL frame for 3D games)
findings.problem: 'The encoder scales, and the HUD moves to a live overlay strip encoded as a second small region' has no possible mechanism. An H.264/MP4 track has one picture per frame, and iPhone Photos, iMessage and WhatsApp will not composite a second region or a second video track. The research concludes 'WebKit has no zero-readback way to overlay a HUD', and nothing in the research supports a 'second small region'. 'The encoder scales' (a full-DPR WebGL frame fed to an encoder configured at 720p) is also asserted, not proven. The storage verifier explicitly asked to 'Test that WebKit's encoder accepts frames whose size differs from the config', and that test is missing from the PR 0.4 lab list.
findings.evidence: GAMEPLAY_CLIPS.html:187. plan-research storage-perf-lifecycle verify.designSpecProblems[0] ('texImage2D(canvas) uses getImageData/copyNativeImage. So WebKit has no zero-readback way to overlay a HUD ... Test that WebKit's encoder accepts frames whose size differs from the config'). PR 0.4 lab list (GAMEPLAY_CLIPS.html:622) measures 'VideoFrame cost for compositor paths A/B/C' but not encoder-side scaling. A grep of both research JSONs finds no 'overlay strip' or 'second small region'.
findings.fix: Rewrite path B with real options only: (a) no HUD in live frames, with score and brag data on the end card; or (b) draw the HUD inside the game's own WebGL render (an R3F overlay scene rendered last into the same canvas, replacing the DOM HUD so the live view and the clip match). Delete 'second small region'. Add to PR 0.4: 'VideoEncoder on WebKit accepts VideoFrame(webglCanvas) larger than config.width/height and scales it (else scale via drawingBufferWidth or a smaller WebGL render target)', with a pass/fail memo line.

findings.problem: Section 3 labels 'a small compositor canvas fixes it' as proven and quotes 'about 15%'. The feasibility spike actually measured Monster Truck falling from 40.4-41.9 fps idle to 33.5-34.1 fps (a 17-19% loss) on an M5 desktop. The compositor also delivered only 45 frames per 2.9 s (about 15 fps, half the 30 fps target). This fails 7's guarantee ('capture never costs the game more than 10% of its frame rate') and both 15.2 thresholds (at most 10% loss; capture at least 90% of target on desktop). It happens on the fastest hardware in the matrix, before any iPhone readback cost. The plan treats desktop Chrome 3D as solved and puts only the iPhone number on the Phase 0 unknown list.
findings.evidence: design/clips/research/feasibility-2026-09-27.json spike evidence: 'Downscaled compositor at 640 and 960 wide: rAF 33.5-34.1 fps (idle 40.4 before, 41.9 after), 45-46 frames per about 2.9 s ... (about 15 fps presented)'. Appendix A group note GAMEPLAY_CLIPS.html:2400 ('about 34 fps through a 960-wide compositor'). Plan :169, :334, and 15.2.
findings.fix: Relabel the section 3 row 'not proven: 17-19% fps loss and ~15 fps effective capture on M5 (captureStream path)'. Add desktop Chrome 3D to the Phase 0 decision memo with the planned VideoFrame+VideoEncoder path, and A/B it against moving the composite off the game thread: transfer VideoFrame(webglCanvas), measured at 0.04 ms main-thread on Chrome, and scale plus HUD-composite it in the worker's OffscreenCanvas (verify missedIssues[3] in the encoding track). State the expected steady-state rung for Monster Truck on each device class, so the 10% gate is not failed by design.

findings.problem: 'Timestamps come from a frame index: ts = round(n * 1e6 / fps)' with 'integer vsync-stride pacing' does not define n when the game misses vsyncs, or when 'Backpressure drops a frame'. If n counts captured frames, then any game that cannot hold the display rate has video time compressed against the wall-clock-locked, sample-counted audio. Monster Truck on the M5 runs 41 fps on a 60 Hz display (rAF is not called every vsync). At stride 2 that gives about 20.5 captures/s stamped as 30 fps, so 30 s of play becomes about 20 s of video under 30 s of audio. The storage verifier said to keep slot pacing 'for irregular game cadences'. The plan dropped that and puts no rule in its place, yet 15.1 tests a 41 Hz clock.
findings.evidence: GAMEPLAY_CLIPS.html:292-300 (6.2), :589 ('capture clock at 30/41/50/60/75/90/120/144 Hz'). feasibility JSON spike: 'Game rAF fell from 40-42 fps idle'. storage-perf-lifecycle DSP 5 ('Keep slot pacing only for irregular game cadences').
findings.fix: Define n from time, not from a counter: n = round((rAFtimestamp − epochStart − removedPauseTime) / (stride × vsyncPeriod)). Measure vsyncPeriod separately from the game's rAF cadence (median of the shortest intervals). If a slot has no new frame (missed vsync, backpressure drop), extend the previous sample's duration and do not advance a counter. If two captures round to the same slot, keep the later one. Add a vitest case: a 41 fps irregular rAF trace over 30 s must yield video duration = audio duration ±1 frame.

findings.section: 4.1 io.worker editor render pass / 6.5 PCM ring
findings.problem: The only PCM source for the editor is the live 'PCM ring (Int16, 62 s) for the editor'. But the editor normally opens on saved My Clips items and auto-highlights, and its features change audio: the Sound tab ducks game audio under music, and speed 2x/slow-mo rewrites timing. For those clips the plan needs an AAC decode path, and iOS 16.4-18.x (tier W+, about 1 iPhone in 5) has no AudioDecoder (research DSP 21, dropped). The editor render pass lives in io.worker, but OfflineAudioContext and AudioContext are Window-only, so the synthesized music loops cannot be rendered there with Web Audio. Re-encoding exports (Tall/Wide re-frame, end card, speed) need a VideoDecoder and a second VideoEncoder while the live ring encoder is kept alive through visible pauses (7.1). On Android that is three concurrent MediaCodec sessions, which is neither budgeted nor sequenced (research DSP 15 and MISS 7, both dropped).
findings.evidence: GAMEPLAY_CLIPS.html:213, 243 (io.worker 'editor render pass'), :325 (PCM ring for the editor), :478 (editor Sound/Style/speed), :353 ('Visible pauses keep the encoder alive'). storage-perf-lifecycle verify.designSpecProblems[15] and missedIssues[7]. encoding-pipeline verify.designSpecProblems[21]. The Web Audio API interfaces are [Exposed=Window] (the plan itself cites OfflineAudioContext only on the main thread, :2432).
findings.fix: Specify editor audio: decode the saved clip's AAC with AudioDecoder where it exists, and otherwise with a WASM aacdec from the same pinned FFmpeg build or main-thread decodeAudioData, into a PCM buffer handed to the render pass. Render music and SFX in a main-thread OfflineAudioContext and transfer the PCM to io.worker. Sequence exports: while the editor sheet is open (the game is paused), flush and close the live encoder, run the export, then re-arm (accepting the new epoch). Add an export memory budget and a Phase 0 probe for concurrent MediaCodec sessions on the Android device.

findings.section: 8.3 Record mode (share-time handling for big files)
findings.problem: The big-file rules cover only Chromium's 50 MiB share cap. On iPhone, WebKit's ShareDataReader reads the whole shared File into memory and then copies it again, so sharing a Record-mode file needs about 2x its size in WebContent memory. At about 23 MB/min (3 Mbps + AAC), a 20-minute recording (about 460 MB) needs about 1 GB and will be jetsammed. That kills the tab mid-share on the platform the plan treats as primary ('Share (share sheet)' for iPhone in section 12). 8.1's 'OPFS getFile() is disk-backed, so previews and shares never copy the whole file into memory' is false for iOS shares. The research flagged this (verify [15], DSP 14), and the plan dropped it.
findings.evidence: encoding-pipeline verify.verdicts[15].correction: 'WebKit ShareDataReader.cpp:52-86 reads each shared file fully into memory with FileReaderLoader ReadAsArrayBuffer, then copies it again with SharedBuffer::create ... will get jetsammed. iOS has a practical cap that must be measured.' GAMEPLAY_CLIPS.html:380 (8.1 claim) and :403 (Chromium-only rule).
findings.fix: Add a Phase 0 measurement of the largest file that shares successfully from the oldest supported iPhone (tab and Home Screen app). Add an iOS row to the share decision table in 8.3 and section 12: above the measured ceiling, offer Trim, the ≥1.2 Mbps smaller copy, split parts under the ceiling, or a hosted link, and never call navigator.share with the oversized file. Correct the 8.1 sentence.

findings.problem: 'Fallback chain: OPFS, then an IndexedDB Blob (Safari private mode throws on OPFS)' fails at step 2 in exactly the case it exists for. Safari private windows also reject putting a Blob into IndexedDB ('Error preparing Blob/File data to be stored in object store'). Private-mode IndexedDB is memory-only anyway, so it adds no durability over the in-memory tier.
findings.evidence: underpassapp.com/news/2025/9/4.html (2025-09-04): 'Safari private windows do not support putting a Blob in an IndexedDB object store ... Error preparing Blob/File data to be stored in object store', and getDirectory() throws in private windows. GAMEPLAY_CLIPS.html:382.
findings.fix: When getDirectory() throws the private-window error, go straight to the in-memory tier with the sticky 'share or save it now' sheet. Keep the IndexedDB tier only for non-private OPFS failures, and store ArrayBuffer chunks rather than Blobs there. Assert the private-tab path in the real-device row of 15.1.

findings.problem: The tier table does not place some browsers that are inside the stated floor (Safari 16.4+/Chrome 111+/Firefox 111+). Firefox desktop 111-129 has no WebCodecs and no MP4 MediaRecorder, so it can only be tier V, but V lists only Firefox Android and 32-bit ARM Chrome. macOS Safari 16.4-18.x (Macs that cannot run Safari 26) has VideoEncoder but no AudioEncoder, so it belongs in W+, but W+ lists only iOS 16.4-18.x. 'Cached per browser build' (4.1) needs a build identifier, while the same row forbids user-agent version tokens. The 6.5 ring 'budget by device class' has no iOS class source, because navigator.deviceMemory is Chromium-only (encoding DSP 12).
findings.evidence: BCD 8.1.3 (/tmp/hh-clips/pkgs/bcd): VideoEncoder firefox 130, AudioEncoder safari 26, VideoEncoder safari 16.4. GAMEPLAY_CLIPS.html:241, 258-266, 324.
findings.fix: Add Firefox desktop 111-129 to tier V and macOS Safari 16.4-18.x to W+. Key the probe cache on a hash of the probe results plus navigator.userAgent as an opaque string (never parsed for versions), or re-probe at every arm and drop the cache. Define the iOS memory class explicitly (for example 'AudioEncoder in self' as the WebKit 26+/A13+ proxy, per storage DSP 6) and give it a conservative default ring budget.

findings.section: 6.5 Clip assembly (audio start and edit lists)
findings.problem: 'It does not depend on an edit list' is not true for the audio track as specified. AAC packets are 1024 samples (21.3 ms) and are shifted by -P/48000 with P=2114. So the first audio packet at or after the video keyframe almost never lands exactly on it. mediabunny 1.60 writes an elst whenever a track's first timestamp is not 0 (an empty edit for a positive offset, a trim for a negative one). The file therefore does carry an audio edit list. Players that ignore it drift up to one AAC frame, and the 5 ms test cannot catch that because ffmpeg and AVFoundation honor the elst.
findings.evidence: mediabunny isobmff-boxes.js trak(): needsEditList = startTimestampOffset !== 0. edts(): a positive offset writes a 2-entry elst with media_time -1, a negative offset writes a trim. isobmff-muxer.js:626-629 (startTimestampOffset = first timestamp). GAMEPLAY_CLIPS.html:326 and :142-143 (priming shift).
findings.fix: State the rule: start audio at the AAC packet whose timestamp is nearest the keyframe instant, and rebase both tracks so video[0]=0 and audio[0]=0 (a fixed shift of at most 10.7 ms, below the BT.1359 bound), so no elst is written. Or accept the audio elst and add an 'elst-ignoring player' check (ExoPlayer 2.x) with the matching tolerance. Include one extra leading AAC packet as decoder pre-roll so the first 21 ms is not a click.

findings.problem: 'Pauses are removed from the timeline ... video and audio are cut at the same boundary' together with 'AAC is encoded continuously' leaves open whether a pause is cut by dropping encoded AAC packets. AAC frames overlap through the MDCT, so splicing packets from two different times gives a transient click at every removed pause, and the PLL/sample counter would jump. 6.4's silence synthesis covers 'live spans' only, so the pause case is unspecified.
findings.evidence: GAMEPLAY_CLIPS.html:298 (pause removal), :316-317 (continuous AAC, synthesized silence for live spans).
findings.fix: Specify that pause removal happens in the PCM domain before the AAC encoder: stop feeding tap samples at the pause boundary, apply a 5-10 ms fade-out and fade-in across the join, and keep the sample counter contiguous, so the encoder never sees a gap and no encoded packet is ever dropped mid-stream.

findings.problem: The replay kit sends offline audio through 'mediabunny AudioBufferSource ... so mediabunny's AAC path and its WebKit-302253 fix apply'. That path uses mediabunny's conditional ASC repair, which 5.1 deliberately replaced with 'ASC always rebuilt' because the repair only fires on missing or objectType-0 descriptions (verify [1]). On iOS 16.4-18.x mediabunny has no AAC encoder at all unless a custom encoder is registered. The plan's WASM build is a self-built FFmpeg 'called directly', not @mediabunny/aac-encoder, so the DOM-replay clips on tier W+ have no stated AAC path.
findings.evidence: encoding-pipeline verify.verdicts[1].correction ('override it unconditionally with ascFor(sr,ch) instead of detecting'). GAMEPLAY_CLIPS.html:272 (5.1), :317 (WASM called directly), :2432 (replay AudioBufferSource).
findings.fix: Route replay audio through the same encoder module as live capture: native AudioEncoder with the unconditional ascFor() override, or the in-house WASM encoder, feeding EncodedAudioPacketSource. Or register the WASM build as a mediabunny CustomAudioEncoder and post-patch the ASC. Add a W+ (iOS 18 simulator) replay-clip case to 15.1.

summary:
I checked sections 11, 12 and 14 against the repo rules, the mobile-playability skill, Jack's anti-slop, STE and data-integrity rules, and the real GameShell, PauseMenu, toast and game HUD code. The plan is thorough on engine mechanics, but the kid-facing flow still has real holes. The biggest one is section 14. It says "sharing a clip is not publishing", so clips of kid-built or kid-changed games skip the identity scrub, even though every such game gets open sharing by default. That breaks the settled "no real names in clips" rule and guardrail 7. On the experience side:
- The in-game path from "Clip saved!" to Watch depends on a "natural break". That break never comes in canPause=false games that have no run end, including every zero-code kid-built game. At the pause break, the toast lane (z-1100) renders under PauseMenu (z-2000).
- Record, Photo, My clips and Clip settings are only reachable by a hidden 500 ms long-press. The research's pause-menu entry and the long-press teaching toast were dropped.
- The recording header state adds controls that the 320-480 px width budget never counts, so the header overflows.
- In-play warming and error toasts are text-only for pre-readers. Almost no game-over screen has the read-aloud button that CLAUDE.md requires, and the chip and coach mark land on those screens.
- The first-best coach mark says "tap to save it" in the same break where the chip says "we saved your new best".
- "Photos" and "Save" each mean two different things in the copy, so a kid looks in the wrong app.
- Auto clips are deleted after an arbitrary 7 days.
- "hankshits.com" is hard-coded in clip frames and the file name, so a kid's rebranded site advertises the wrong site.
- Copied or remixed DOM games carry their sibling's clipRenderer, and no test checks that it matches the live game.
- A guest note tells kids to "Sign in to get a player name", which pushes them into the signup the plan itself flags as a COPPA gap.
- Monster Truck's TILT and CALIBRATE buttons already sit under the header, right where the clapper cluster goes.

The minor items are test coverage gaps, copy that contradicts the plan's own state machine, and smaller gaps in the header, trim and read-aloud specs.

findings.section: 14 Kid-built games get clips by default (put-it-online edit)
findings.problem: Clips of kid-built and kid-changed games skip the identity scrub. The repo relies on that scrub as its only backstop for names put into a game. The clip privacy test also cannot catch literal names in canvas.
findings.evidence: Section 14: every game gets clips unless metadata says clips: false, and put-it-online is edited to say "sharing a clip is not publishing; the scrub covers text drawn into canvas". Section 2 settles "No real names in clips" and says "Safety comes from what a clip can contain". Section 12 opens the share sheet with no gate, and section 1 says the MP4 plays on YouTube. put-it-online/SKILL.md:51 expects names in local games: "a kid may have asked you earlier to put their name/school into a game, this is where you catch it". change-a-game/SKILL.md has no identity rule. The section 10 source-scan test only flags strings that flow from an <input> into fillText or a CanvasTexture, so a literal like "Beat Liam!" or "Grandma Sue's Farm" that Claude writes into a canvas passes. Section 13.2 gates only HOSTED links on the scrub, not the share sheet.
findings.fix: Make the clip content gate part of the game, not of who shares it. Option 1: kid-built games (madeByKid: true) default to clips: false until the put-it-online identity scrub has run, recorded as a literal (for example clipsScrubbed: true) that the scrub step writes. Option 2: move the scrub to build time in make-a-game, change-a-game and remix-a-game, and add a source-scan test that fails when a kid-built clip-enabled game draws any string literal that is not in an allowlist (game name, UI words). Either way, delete "sharing a clip is not publishing", add the rule to the CLAUDE.md New Game checklist, and add a Phase 8 exit test in which a change-a-game request adds a friend's name and the clip gate fails.

findings.problem: The Watch button, the highlight chip and the coach mark only appear at a "natural break". Several real games never have one, and neither does any zero-code kid-built game. In those games a kid sees "Clip saved!" and has no visible way to watch or share the clip without leaving the game. The plan also never says what a manual clip shows at the break: the toast lasts 4 s, while anti-nag allows one chip per run.
findings.evidence: 11.1: "The saved toast is non-interactive during active play. Its Watch button appears at the next break" (run end, result screen, pause). These games have canPause={false} and no run end: app/games/cookie-clicker/page.tsx:29, app/games/four-wheeler-adventure/page.tsx:36, app/games/retro-arcade/page.tsx:30, games/four-wheeler-3d/GameShell.tsx:29. make-a-game/SKILL.md:56 makes canPause={false} the default for every new kid game, and 11.5 says the shell learns run boundaries only through runPhase(), which a zero-code game never calls. The toast lasts SHOW_MS = 4000 (AchievementCelebrations.tsx:13). 11.5 allows "at most one chip per run and one per 3 minutes", so the plan cannot deliver Watch for a manual clip at a later break.
findings.fix: Define a third path that needs no break. After a manual clip, keep a small persistent "new clip" badge on the clapper until it is watched. A plain tap on the badged clapper at any time opens the newest clip; for canPause=false games, suspend the ring and freeze input under the sheet, and warn with the anti-punish copy if a run would end. Specify what a manual clip shows at a break (a persistent chip exempt from the one-per-run cap), and make auto-discovery treat a best-score change or a GameStartOverlay remount as run end for zero-code games.

findings.section: 11.4 Toast lane / 11.1 natural breaks / Appendix A (g)
findings.problem: At the pause break, the toast lane renders under the pause menu, so the Watch button and the highlight chip cannot be seen or tapped. The adopted research spec also forbids chips while a pause menu, start card or modal is up. That removes every break the plan lists. A third conflicting surface, the "result share chip", exists only in Appendix A and uses a different z-order.
findings.evidence: The toast lane is AchievementCelebrations at "fixed inset-x-0 top-14 z-[1100]" (AchievementCelebrations.tsx:73), and research ux-prior-art designSpec 4.1 keeps z-[1100]. PauseMenu is "fixed inset-0 z-[2000] ... bg-black/85" (PauseMenu.tsx:62). 11.1 lists "pause" as a natural break. Research designSpec 4.5(e): "Chips never appear while a start card, pause menu, or modal is up". Most games paint their game-over card as a modal-like overlay (flappy-bird/Game.tsx:188-230). Appendix A (g): "The result share chip must be DOM ... above z-50 ... and below the GameShell header (z-1000)". Section 11 never defines that chip.
findings.fix: Write one stacking and placement contract in 11.4. At pause, render the clip entry INSIDE PauseMenu through the children slot plus spokenExtras (the research's "🎬 Clips" button, which the plan dropped). At a result screen, use the Appendix A result chip, defined once in section 11 with its z-index, position and read-aloud. Rewrite 4.5(e) so it matches, and record the order in the ARCHITECTURE.md stacking update that section 14 already promises.

findings.problem: The recording state adds a red stop control and a timer pill next to the star button, but the width budget never counts them. The header overflows on common phones while recording, and no test covers that state.
findings.evidence: 11.3 Recording: "Clapper becomes a star-bookmark button; red stop control and a \"0:42\" pill beside it". GameShell.tsx:69-131 uses px-3 (24 px), a 44 px home button, a title with px-2 (16 px) plus the 28 px emoji, and 44 px controls. A canPause=false guest game (for example flappy) at 360 px, after steps 1, 2 and 4, is 24 + 44 + 44 + [star 44 + stop 44 + pill about 48 + 🏆 44 + ⛶ 44 + ↻ 44 + Sign In 44] = 424 px. That is over 360, and also over 412. Step 5 only runs below 340 px. The 15.2 header check covers "guest and signed-in, pausable and not" with no recording row.
findings.fix: Keep recording within one slot, as the research spec did. The red stop replaces the clapper in the header, and bookmarks go on a separate star button in the toast lane, or the reverse. Move the timer pill under the header, at the left of the toast lane. Then add "recording" and "saving" rows to the 15.2 header matrix at every width.

findings.problem: On a phone, Record a video, Take a photo, My clips from this game and Clip settings can only be reached with a hidden 500 ms long-press or a right-click. Below 340 px, Fullscreen is hidden there too. The research's visible pause-menu entry and its long-press teaching tip were both dropped. A 6-year-old's slow tap also turns into the long-press, so the clip is not saved.
findings.evidence: 11.2: "Long-press (500 ms) or right-click opens the Capture menu" and "Below 340 px: Fullscreen moves into the clapper's long-press Capture menu". Research designSpec section 1 had "Pause menu (canPause games): one new full-width button '🎬 Clips' ... Add 'Clips' to spokenExtras" and 9.4 "Long-press teaching, once, after the 3rd manual clip". Neither is in the plan (grep of sections 11 and 16 finds neither). NN/g, Children's UX: Physical Development (nngroup.com/articles/children-ux-physical-development): "the game did support a nondrag interaction ... but none of the kids in our study discovered that feature." The mobile-playability skill fails hidden-only paths ("Nothing is hover-gated").
findings.fix: Add a visible entry to every in-game surface. Put a "🎬 Clips" button in PauseMenu with spokenExtras, and put a Record/Photo row in the result chip for canPause=false games. Bring back the one-time teaching tip, spoken via read-aloud. Fire Clip it on pointerdown, not on release, so a slow press still saves, and open the menu only on a real hold. Move Fullscreen below 340 px into the pause menu or a visible overflow button, not into a gesture menu on an unrelated control.

findings.section: 11.1 Read-aloud everywhere / 11.3 Warming and Error states
findings.problem: The toasts that tell a kid WHY nothing happened (warming, error, resting) appear during play, where the plan makes toasts non-interactive, and ReadAloudButton only speaks when tapped. So a pre-reader gets these instructions as text only, which the house rule forbids. The plan also contradicts itself: every toast has a ReadAloudButton, but toasts cannot be tapped during play.
findings.evidence: 11.1: "Every sheet, toast and empty state has a ReadAloudButton" versus "The saved toast is non-interactive during active play". ReadAloudButton.tsx:8: "It speaks only when the player taps it. It never speaks on its own". 11.3 Warming: "Hint: 'Play a little first! Then tap the clapper again.'" Error: "Toast with the reason in kid words". The lane is pointer-events-none (AchievementCelebrations.tsx:73). Repo CLAUDE.md: "Never make an important instruction text-only. Show it, say it, or point at the button."
findings.fix: Toasts that answer the kid's own clapper tap (warming, error, resting) keep a pointer-events-auto 44 px 🔊 button, exempt from the non-interactive rule because the kid just tapped for them. Also make warming visible without words: the ring fills over 3 s and a tap during warming pulses the ring once, with no motion when reduced motion is on. Rewrite 11.1 so it states which toasts get read-aloud and when.

findings.problem: The highlight chip and the first-run coach mark appear on game-over screens, but almost no game has the read-aloud button that CLAUDE.md requires on the restart screen. Section 17 does not list this pre-existing defect, even though PR 1.3 already edits every game-over card.
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:29: "Every game has a big 🔊 'Read it to me' button on its start screen, pause screen, and restart screen". GameStartOverlay (which carries the read-aloud) mounts only on ready or idle states in all 24 games that use it (for example flappy-bird/Game.tsx:391 `gameState === "ready"`). Game-over is painted into the canvas with no speech (flappy-bird/Game.tsx:188-230 "Game Over!"). Among the games, ReadAloudButton appears only in four-wheeler-3d, retro-arcade, hill-climb/ui/PauseMenu.tsx and monster-truck GameUI.
findings.fix: Add this defect class to section 17 and PR 1.3. Every result or game-over card gets a DOM ReadAloudButton that speaks the result, the Play Again control, and (after Phase 2) the clip chip. Put it in the same DOM chip layer that Appendix A (g) already needs, so each game gets it with one mount.

findings.section: 11.4 First run coach mark vs 11.1 / 11.5 auto-highlights
findings.problem: At the first new best, the kid gets two opposite messages at the same break: the chip says "We saved your new best!" while the coach mark says "Tap the clapper to save it!". Tapping at game over also saves the last 30 s, which may not contain the record moment. The result is a duplicate clip and a lesson that teaches the wrong thing.
findings.evidence: 11.4: "one coach mark at the first new best: 'You just beat your best! Tap the clapper to save it!'". 11.5: "the achievements personal-best watermark gives every game a 'new best' highlight", and featured moments auto-clip "8 s before to 3 s after". 11.1: the "we saved your new best" chip appears at a natural break. 11.5 itself says "the old best was passed 40 s ago", which is outside a 30 s clip taken at game over.
findings.fix: Trigger the coach mark on the first run where the kid did NOT get an auto clip (or the first run longer than about 20 s), and word it for the future: "Next time something cool happens, tap 🎬!". At the first new best, show only the highlight chip and teach the clapper on its Watch screen. Add a test that the two never share a break.

findings.problem: The copy uses one word for two different things, so a kid looks in the wrong place. "Photo saved!" means saved in My Clips, while "Save to Photos" means Apple's Photos app. "Save" means saving to the library, downloading, iOS Save Video and Keep. The capture button has three names. This breaks Jack's STE rule for UI copy (one word, one meaning).
findings.evidence: Research copy deck (adopted by 11.6): "photo: 'Photo saved! 📸' [See it]" and the My Clips filter "📸 Photos". Plan 8.2: "always offers 'Save to Photos'", "Save favorites to Photos!". Research 6.3: "Want it in Photos? Tap Share, then tap Save Video." The 11.3 toast "Clip saved!" sits beside the 12 buttons "Save to phone" and "Save to computer". The button is called "the clapper" (11.3, 11.4), "the clip button" (research 9.1) and 🎬, while the 11.6 glossary lists only "clip camera". 8.1 also says "shelf" for My Clips. ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md documentation-style extends ASD-STE100 "one word = one meaning" to UI copy.
findings.fix: Put one term per concept in the 11.6 glossary. Rename in-app stills to "pictures" ("Picture saved in My Clips!") and keep "Photos" only for the phone's Photos app. Use "Keep" for the library ("Clip kept!"). Use "Save to phone" and "Save to Photos" only for copies that leave the site. Pick one name for the button ("clip button 🎬") and use it in every string, including the warming hint and the coach mark. Add a copy test that fails when a banned synonym appears.

findings.problem: Auto clips are deleted after 7 days even when there is plenty of storage. That is an arbitrary time cap on the kid's own highlights, and Jack's data-integrity rule forbids it. Combined with the anti-nag mute, a weekend player loses every highlight they never saw. The notice about it is text-only.
findings.evidence: 8.1: "Caps are justified by storage: at most 25% of the quota estimate ... Auto clips expire after 7 days unless kept." The storage budget already carries the real limit, so the 7-day rule has no constraint behind it. 11.5: "Three ignored chips mute chips for that game for 7 days (saving continues silently into the Auto filter)." ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md data-integrity: "NEVER impose an arbitrary size/count/time cap that silently drops data ... justify it against a REAL constraint."
findings.fix: Remove the 7-day timer. Evict unkept auto clips oldest first only when the library passes its 25% budget. Before any eviction, show the kept list and give a spoken 🔊 notice, and never remove a clip marked NEW (unwatched). Update the research copy ("Auto clips clean up after a week") to match.

findings.section: 14 Kid-built games / 11.4 end card / 12 file name / 13 hosted page
